questions.prompt: Why is frequent repetition alone insufficient to identify a disorder?
questions.answer: Function, clinical context, difficulty controlling behaviour, distress and impact may differ.
Interference with important areas of ordinary functioning.
questions.feedback: Describe an effect without diagnosing its cause.

questions.prompt: Does physical dependence necessarily establish addiction?
questions.answer: No; physiological adaptation can occur without addiction.
questions.feedback: Distinguish the mechanism from a behavioural diagnosis.

questions.prompt: What is the learner's role when impairment is reported?
questions.answer: Offer proportionate support and encourage qualified assessment, rather than diagnosing or treating.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer, formative only; use specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Distinguishes routine, possible compulsion, reported impairment and physical dependence without diagnosing; identifies appropriate support.
scoring.transfer: Construct two fictional descriptions with similar repetition but different functions and impacts. Produce a neutral comparison and one appropriate referral option. Identify three pieces of information that are unknown rather than speculating.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; never average away missing or safety-critical evidence. Quizzes cannot certify competence.
